trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
Going up-right would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes down-right.
Going right would force the line onto number 16 before its turn; going down-right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes down-left.
Going left, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (-1,3); going right leaves no safe move afterwards (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes down-left.
I can't rule out up-left or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up-left.
Number 4 is only reachable this way.
Number 5 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going up-left, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes left.
Number 8 is only reachable this way.
Number 9 is only reachable this way.
Number 10 is only reachable this way.
Going down-right would leave number 11 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going to number 11 leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes left.
Number 11 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going down-right would turn number 13 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes down-left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.

Going up-right would turn number 15 into a dead-end pocket with no way out; going right would leave both cell (3,-3) and number 16 needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes up-left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going left would leave both number 18 and number 21 needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes up-left.
Going down-left would force the line onto number 21 before its turn. So the line goes left.
Going down-right would force the line onto number 21 before its turn. So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down-right.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
